executive_summary: Architecture health is 6.5/10 — functionally robust in the risk engine and kill-switch layers, but structurally over-engineered with 708 .py files across three conflicting strategy locations and three registries sharing the same name. The critical MT5 handle bug and 109-file legacy strategy dump were fixed between audits, proving the team can execute on issues. However, the architecture suffers from premature abstraction, scattered test directories, a bloated .gitignore, Docker configs that don't match reality, and a CI pipeline that tests on Linux while deploying to Windows. The most dangerous remaining issue is silent fallback masking: the `__getattr__` pattern in `engine/__init__.py` and blanket `try/except` wrappers throughout the codebase mean import errors, method-not-found, and misconfigurations fail silently — producing a system that appears to work (no crashes) but actually does nothing (loss veto reads 0.0 forever, strategies silently skipped, etc.). This is a production system that needs surgical architectural consolidation, not feature growth.

critical_findings.finding: `__all__` lists `standalone` which does not exist anywhere in `quant_nanggroe/engine/` or `quant_nanggroe/`. The `__getattr__` fallback on line 28 silently raises `AttributeError` instead of failing at import time, meaning `from quant_nanggroe.engine import standalone` appears to succeed but holds `None` — downstream code that expects a module gets a broken reference with no warning.
critical_findings.fix: Remove `'standalone'` from `__all__` (line 17). The `pyproject.toml` script entry `qna-standalone = "quant_nanggroe.standalone:main"` (line 108) is also dead and will fail on install.
critical_findings.impact: Silently broken import that no test catches. If any code path ever calls `quant_nanggroe.engine.standalone`, it crashes at call time, not import time — harder to debug.

critical_findings.finding: The `__getattr__` pattern for lazy submodule imports masks ALL import errors — not just the stale `__all__` entries but any future module rename, deletion, or circular dependency. Every failed import silently becomes `AttributeError` indistinguishable from a genuine missing attribute. This creates an invisible maintenance tax where every refactor must manually audit all callers because the runtime provides zero feedback.
critical_findings.fix: Remove `__getattr__` and list only existing modules in `__all__`. Use explicit imports at point of use (callers already import each submodule directly). The lazy pattern provides zero benefit — no circular imports exist in the remaining valid modules.
critical_findings.impact: Any future broken import will silently degrade the system. A renamed `decision.py` would never be noticed until a live trade depends on it.

critical_findings.finding: The MT5 handle fix documented in ARCHITECTURE.md and CHANGELOG.md as P0 is VERIFIED FIXED — line 85 now correctly calls `em._risk_manager.set_broker_handle(mt5)`. This finding is included for completeness: the previous CRITICAL issue (daily/weekly veto reading 0.0) is resolved.
critical_findings.impact: Previously CRITICAL (loss veto never triggered). Now resolved.

high_findings.finding: Triple Registry architecture with severe naming collision. Two different classes named `StrategyRegistry` exist: one in `engine/strategies/registry.py` (decorator-based strategy class registration) and a completely different one in `engine/strategy/registry.py` (walk-forward metadata tracking). A third registry pattern exists in `hedge_fund/signals/registry.py`. Code importing `StrategyRegistry` from different paths gets different semantics with zero warning.
high_findings.fix: Rename `engine/strategy/registry.py`'s class to `WalkForwardRegistry` or `StrategyMetaRegistry` (an alias already exists at line 321). Consolidate all three registries behind a single interface. Add `__init__.py` re-exports so old imports degrade with a deprecation warning, not silent wrong behavior.
high_findings.impact: A developer importing `from quant_nanggroe.engine.strategy.registry import StrategyRegistry` gets a walk-forward metadata store, but `from quant_nanggroe.engine.strategies.registry import StrategyRegistry` gets a class-registration decorator. Same name, different behavior — a recipe for production bugs.

high_findings.finding: Third strategy location at package root `quant_nanggroe/strategies/` re-exports from `quant_nanggroe.engine.strategy.strategies` (the LEGACY path, not the canonical `engine/strategies/`). The docstring incorrectly states 'All strategies live in quant_nanggroe/engine/strategy/strategies/' when the canonical location is `engine/strategies/`. This re-export chain is fragile and misleading.
high_findings.fix: Update `quant_nanggroe/strategies/__init__.py` to re-export from `quant_nanggroe.engine.strategies` (canonical path), not the legacy shim. Fix the docstring. Alternatively, remove the top-level `strategies/` entirely and update the 3 files that import from it (`backtest_pipeline.py`, and any hedge_fund references).
high_findings.impact: New strategies added to `engine/strategies/` may not be reachable via the top-level package path, breaking code that imports from `quant_nanggroe.strategies`.

high_findings.finding: Version mismatch: `@click.version_option(version="5.1.0", prog_name="qnai")` reports v5.1.0 while the actual system version is v6.1.0 (defined in `qna.py`, `pyproject.toml`, and `__init__.py`). This is a full major+minor version off.
high_findings.fix: Change `version="5.1.0"` to `version="6.1.0"` on `cli.py:41`. Better yet, import `__version__` from `quant_nanggroe` to prevent future drift.
high_findings.impact: Users running `qnai --version` see a version 3 releases behind reality, causing confusion during debugging and support.

high_findings.finding: Legacy `engine/strategy/` directory still contains 12 files and 3 subdirectories beyond the compat shim, including `base_strategy.py`, `self_finetune.py`, `backtest_adapter.py`, `loader.py`, `multi_timeframe.py`, `parser.py`, `regime_strategy.py`, `schema.py`, `strategy_selector.py`, `templates/`, and `registry.py` (the walk-forward one). These are never loaded by the active system but create confusion about which strategy path is canonical.
high_findings.fix: Delete all files from `engine/strategy/` except `__init__.py` (the compat shim) and `strategies/__init__.py` (the re-export shim). Move the walk-forward registry (`engine/strategy/registry.py`) to `engine/backtest/walkforward_registry.py` if it is actively used.
high_findings.impact: Maintenance burden: any new developer will waste time understanding which strategy path matters. Dead code paths may accumulate bugs without detection.

high_findings.finding: CI only runs on `ubuntu-latest` but the primary deployment target is Windows (MT5 only runs on Windows, DNSBypass module is Windows-specific, launch scripts target cmd.exe). Linux CI cannot test MT5 connectivity, broker wiring, or the 25+ Windows-specific code paths.
high_findings.fix: Add a Windows runner matrix entry: `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}` with `matrix.os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]`. Skip MT5-dependent tests on Linux with pytest marks.
high_findings.impact: A Windows-only regression (e.g., path separator bug in builder.py, DNSBypass SSL failure, cmd.exe launch script breakage) will pass CI and only fail in production.

medium_findings.finding: Imports from `quant_nanggroe.strategies.tsmom` (top-level strategies path) instead of the canonical `quant_nanggroe.engine.strategies`. This is the only file importing from the top-level path, creating an invisible dependency on the legacy re-export chain.
medium_findings.fix: Update imports to use `quant_nanggroe.engine.strategies.tsmom_strategy` or the StrategyRegistry pattern.
medium_findings.impact: If the top-level `strategies/` is removed or the re-export chain breaks, the backtest gate silently fails.

medium_findings.finding: Redundant `pip install`: `pip install -e ".[dev]"` already installs pytest and pytest-cov (defined in `[dev]` deps in `pyproject.toml` lines 98-100). The second `pip install pytest pytest-cov` re-installs the same packages, wasting 15-30 seconds per CI run.
medium_findings.fix: Remove line 12 (`pip install pytest pytest-cov`). The `[dev]` dependency group already covers it.
medium_findings.impact: Minimal, but the redundancy suggests CI config was written without understanding the dependency tree — carelessness in infrastructure that hints at deeper process issues.

medium_findings.finding: Worker service command runs `python -m quant_nanggroe.engine.worker` but `engine/worker.py` is a module file, not a runnable package. The `if __name__ == "__main__"` block may exist, but the path `quant_nanggroe.engine.worker` resolves to `quant_nanggroe/engine/worker.py` which has no CLI entry point — the file is a `BackgroundWorker` class definition, not a script.
medium_findings.fix: Change the worker command to `["python", "qna.py", "daemon"]` or provide a proper `__main__` block in `worker.py`. Verify the worker actually starts and processes tasks in Docker.
medium_findings.impact: The worker container will crash-loop on startup, consuming resources and logging confusing errors.

medium_findings.finding: Hardcoded database credentials in version control: `sqlalchemy.url = postgresql://qna:qna_dev_password@localhost:5432/quant_nanggroe`. The comment correctly says the URL should come from `DATABASE_URL` env var, but the default value contains a real password pattern.
medium_findings.fix: Remove the hardcoded URL and use only env-var substitution: `sqlalchemy.url = %(DATABASE_URL)s`. Document the required env var in `.env.example`.
medium_findings.impact: Credential leak if the repo is ever public or shared. Also, the hardcoded default is wrong for any real deployment.

medium_findings.finding: Bloated and duplicated entries. `graphify-out/` appears twice (lines 114, 127). `node_modules/` appears twice (lines 67, 132). `config/mt5_accounts.yaml` appears three times (lines 139, 140-141, 153). `*.db` and `test_qna.db` overlap with database entries (lines 55-58). The file is hard to audit for missing entries.
medium_findings.fix: Deduplicate and reorganize. Remove duplicate lines. Merge overlapping patterns. Group by category with clear headers. Target 60-80 lines.
medium_findings.impact: None functionally, but the bloat suggests rushed maintenance — and a bloated gitignore is a sign of architectural neglect.

medium_findings.finding: Inconsistent environment variable naming conventions. Uses `QNAI_*` prefix for most vars (e.g., `QNAI_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `QNAI_REDIS_URL`) but the codebase also uses `QNA_*` prefix (`QNA_KILL_SWITCH_STATE_FILE`, `QNA_LIVE_TRADING`, `QNA_MACRO_WEATHER`, `QNA_UNIFIED_MODE`). Critical runtime vars like `QNA_KILL_SWITCH_STATE_FILE`, `QNA_LIVE_TRADING`, and `QNA_UNIFIED_MODE` are not documented in `.env.example`.
medium_findings.fix: Consolidate to a single prefix (either `QNAI_` or `QNA_`). Add all documented env vars to `.env.example` with appropriate sections. Document the QNA_* env vars used by `qna.py` for causal macro context and kill switch.
medium_findings.impact: Operators cannot discover required configuration from `.env.example` alone. Critical safety vars (`QNA_LIVE_TRADING`) are undocumented.

medium_findings.finding: Two test directories with different conventions. The core test suite is in `tests/` (81 entries) but the DCC-GARCH tests (47 tests) are in `quant_nanggroe/tests/`. The DCC-GARCH tests are `pyproject.toml`'s second `testpaths` entry, making them a second-class citizen that new developers may not discover.
medium_findings.fix: Move `quant_nanggroe/tests/test_dcc_garch.py` and `quant_nanggroe/tests/test_engine_price_provider.py` into the main `tests/` directory with appropriate subdirectory structure. Remove `quant_nanggroe/tests` from `testpaths` in `pyproject.toml`.
medium_findings.impact: Minor organizational debt. A developer running `pytest tests/` (as documented in AGENTS.md) will miss the DCC-GARCH tests.

medium_findings.finding: Uses deprecated `version: "3.9"` key. Docker Compose v2 (the current standard) ignores this key with a warning. The compose file will still work but generates noise.
medium_findings.fix: Remove the `version` key entirely (Docker Compose v2+ ignores it).
medium_findings.impact: Zero functional impact, but noisy warnings suggest the Docker setup was written once and never updated.

medium_findings.finding: Legacy `base_strategy.py` still exists in the shim directory with its own `BaseStrategy` ABC. Even though the `__init__.py` re-exports alias `BaseStrategy = Strategy`, the actual file `base_strategy.py` sits there as dead code that may confuse developers into thinking it's the active base class.
medium_findings.fix: Delete `base_strategy.py` from `engine/strategy/strategies/`. The shim `__init__.py` re-exports are sufficient.
medium_findings.impact: None — the file is never imported directly by any active code.

medium_findings.finding: CI has no linting or type-checking step despite both `ruff` and `mypy` being configured in `pyproject.toml` and documented in `AGENTS.md`. Only tests are run. Given 708 .py files, type errors accumulate silently in CI.
medium_findings.fix: Add `run: ruff check .` and `run: mypy quant_nanggroe/` steps before or after tests. Consider using `--ignore-missing-imports` for mypy to avoid third-party import failures.
medium_findings.impact: Type and lint issues that would be caught by local `pre-commit` are not enforced in CI, allowing bad code to merge.

low_findings.finding: Unused import: `from typing import Generator` is imported but never used in any fixture type hint.
`os` module imported twice — once on line 15 and again on line 28. The second import shadows the first.
low_findings.fix: Remove the redundant `import os` on line 28.

low_findings.finding: File handle leak: `Path("data/evolve_halt_warnings.txt").open("a").write(...)` opens a file without using a context manager (`with` statement). The file handle is only closed by CPython's `__del__` during garbage collection, which is not guaranteed across Python implementations or when exceptions occur.
low_findings.impact: On Windows (the deployment target), leaked file handles can prevent file deletion/rotation. Under high-frequency evolution triggers, this can exhaust file descriptors.

low_findings.finding: `_mock_backtest()` uses random ±30% jitter on ALL metrics for mutation validation. This means the acceptance gate can pass or fail based on random chance, not actual signal quality improvement.
low_findings.fix: Replace with a real walk-forward backtest call, or at minimum reduce jitter to ±1% and add a deterministic seed derived from strategy parameters so repeated evaluations are consistent.
low_findings.impact: Strategy evolution may accept worthless mutations at random, degrading portfolio performance over time.
low_findings.status: FIXED in v6.2.0 — `_real_backtest()` now uses `WalkForwardAnalyzer.analyze_strategy()` with per-fold strategy re-fit and OOS Sharpe validation.

low_findings.finding: Docstring incorrectly states 'All strategies live in quant_nanggroe/engine/strategy/strategies/' — this is the LEGACY shim path, not the canonical `engine/strategies/` path. Misleading for developers.

`.gitignore` references paths like `/quant_nanggroe/scripts/` and `/quant_nanggroe/database/alembic.ini` that no longer exist in the repo structure (scripts were archived, database was restructured). These are dead ignore rules that clutter the file.
low_findings.fix: Audit all `.gitignore` paths against current repo structure. Remove any that reference non-existent files/directories.

low_findings.finding: Worker service has no healthcheck and binds no ports — this is correct for a background worker, but also means Docker Compose has no way to detect if the worker is alive. Combined with the broken worker command (see MEDIUM finding), this ensures the worker silently crash-loops.
low_findings.fix: Add a healthcheck to the worker service that checks for its PID file or a health endpoint. Or remove the worker service if it's not functionally used.
low_findings.impact: The worker service will crash-loop without any signal to the operator.

low_findings.finding: Legacy `self_finetune.py` still exists in the shim directory. This was part of the old strategy system and is never loaded in the active architecture.
low_findings.fix: Delete the file. The strategy evolver in `engine/strategies/strategy_evolver.py` is the active self-evolution mechanism.

upgrade_recommendations.recommendation: Eliminate `__getattr__` pattern from `engine/__init__.py` and fix stale `__all__`
upgrade_recommendations.why: Silent fallback masking is the single most dangerous pattern in this codebase. Every import error becomes invisible. Remove `standalone` from `__all__`, remove `__getattr__`, let Python's normal import machinery fail loudly.

upgrade_recommendations.recommendation: Consolidate three strategy locations into one canonical path
upgrade_recommendations.why: `engine/strategies/` (canonical), `engine/strategy/strategies/` (legacy shim), and `quant_nanggroe/strategies/` (top-level re-export) create confusion that leads to duplicate work, missed strategies, and subtle import bugs. Keep only `engine/strategies/`.

Two classes named `StrategyRegistry` with completely different semantics is a landmine. Rename the walk-forward registry, add type-stability tests that verify the correct registry is returned for each import path.

The system's primary deployment target is Windows (MT5 dependency), but CI only tests on Linux. Every Windows-only regression (path handling, SSL context, process management, broker wiring) passes CI and hits production.

upgrade_recommendations.recommendation: Fix Docker compose worker command and add healthchecks
upgrade_recommendations.why: The worker service command is broken (non-existent module path) and the worker has no healthcheck. The entire Docker deployment is non-functional for the worker role.

upgrade_recommendations.recommendation: Fix `cli.py` version pin and import from single source of truth
upgrade_recommendations.why: Version mismatch (5.1.0 vs 6.1.0) creates user confusion. Import `__version__` from `quant_nanggroe` so all version references are automatically synchronized.

Dual `QNAI_*` and `QNA_*` prefixes are confusing and error-prone. Pick one (recommend `QNA_*` since that's what the entry point `qna.py` uses) and migrate all vars. Update `.env.example` to document ALL required vars.
47 DCC-GARCH tests hidden in a non-standard location will be missed by developers running `pytest tests/`. Consolidate to one test root.

upgrade_recommendations.recommendation: Add linting and type-checking to CI pipeline
upgrade_recommendations.why: Ruff and mypy are configured but never run in CI. Add them as quality gates to prevent style and type regressions.

upgrade_recommendations.recommendation: Audit and fix all `try/except Exception` blanket swallows
upgrade_recommendations.why: The codebase has a pervasive pattern of wrapping every import and initialization in `try/except Exception: pass` or `logger.debug`. This makes the system appear resilient while actually masking failures. Every catch should have a minimum `logger.warning` with the exception details, and critical system functions (kill switch, risk gates, broker wiring) should never be silently caught.
153 lines with duplicates indicates a maintenance hygiene issue. Clean it up to 60-80 lines as a symbolic commitment to architectural discipline.
12 files and 131 KB of dead code in a confusing location. Move the walk-forward registry to a proper home; delete everything else.

upgrade_recommendations.recommendation: Fix `strategy_evolver.py` file handle leak and mock backtest
upgrade_recommendations.why: Leaked file handles on Windows can exhaust descriptors under load. The random jitter backtest makes strategy evolution a coin flip.
upgrade_recommendations.status: FIXED in v6.2.0/v6.2.1 — file handle leak fixed with context manager, mock backtest replaced with real walk-forward.

debate_notes: I disagree with several architectural decisions in this codebase. First, the `__getattr__` lazy import pattern in `engine/__init__.py` is solving a problem that doesn't exist — Python already has lazy module loading via `importlib.import_module()` at the call site, which is what every consumer already does. The pattern adds zero value while masking every import error. Remove it entirely. Second, the split between `engine/strategy/` and `engine/strategies/` (singular vs plural) was a terrible namespace choice that will cause confusion for every developer who touches this code. The naming collision on `StrategyRegistry` across these two paths is the concrete consequence. Third, the codebase is over-engineered at 708 .py files for what is ultimately a trading system with ~20 active strategies and ~risk modules. The backtest, walk-forward, factor model, and visualization subpackages each have 19+ files for what could be 3-5 well-organized modules. This fragmentation makes the system harder to reason about, not easier. Fourth, the Docker setup feels bolted on post-hoc — the worker command that doesn't exist, the missing healthcheck, the Linux-only CI for a Windows-targeted system. Either commit to Docker as a first-class deployment target (with proper Windows container support or cross-compilation) or remove it. Half-measures in deployment infrastructure are more dangerous than no infrastructure because they create false confidence. Fifth, the pervasive `try/except Exception` pattern throughout the codebase (every import, every service init, every broker connection) creates a system that silently does nothing when it breaks. A kill switch that reads 0.0 forever because `attach_mt5_handle` raised `AttributeError` that was caught by `except Exception` — this is the system in miniature. Production systems should fail fast and fail loud. The current philosophy of 'never crash' guarantees 'never work correctly'.
verification_notes: Prior audit findings 1 (hermes_* in __all__) and 2 (attach_mt5_handle bug) were VERIFIED FIXED in this session. The 109-file legacy strategy directory was VERIFIED REDUCED to 3 .py files since the prior audit. However, the prior audit claimed 95%+ of Round 2 issues were fixed — this assessment disagrees based on the structural issues that remain (triple registry, dual strategy locations, CI mismatch, over-engineering) which are architectural, not cosmetic.
